conceptZh: 豬探長踮著高高的腳步、吱吱作響地偷偷靠近打瞌睡的玩具海盜，想用大放大鏡看清楚他身後蜘蛛網上的小蜘蛛，結果鸚鵡停在豬探長的鼻子上，海盜一醒，兩人面對面大叫，慌亂中一頭撞上，紅色毛線蛛網被撞散，落下來剛好排成「蛛」字。
object: a bright red yarn spiderweb strung between two short posts behind a dozing barrel-shaped toy pirate, with a tiny friendly cartoon spider in the middle
morph: The head-on bonk between the pig detective and the pirate snaps the red yarn web; its loose strands fly up and drop into place as the 12 strokes of 蛛: the left part 虫 (a small box on a vertical with a rising tick and dot) and the right part 朱 (a slanted top stroke, two horizontals, a long vertical, and the two falling side strokes).
creativeAngle: 這次不是一般的「蜘蛛等蟲子」，而是偵探來查一條線索：線索本身就是蜘蛛網，蛛網的毛線就是字的筆畫，所以撞擊打散蛛網、落下來排成字，看起來很合理。鸚鵡不配合，偏偏停在豬探長的鼻子上，害他打噴嚏把海盜吵醒，這就是驚嚇的原因。蜘蛛畫得小小的、很友善，最後垂著絲掛在字旁邊揮手，剛好對上唸出的「蜘蛛」。
promptEn:
An 8-second bright cartoon slapstick clip on a pale cream background with soft pastel floorboards and nothing busy behind. Teaching glyph: 蛛.

0–1.5s: A stout cartoon detective pig in a checked deerstalker hat hops into frame from the left, raising a giant magnifying glass. He gasps and points: center-right, a bright red yarn spiderweb hangs between two short posts, a tiny round friendly spider in the middle. Below it a barrel-shaped toy pirate snores with his eye patch pushed up, and a green parrot perches on his hat.

1.5–3s: The pig tiptoes in exaggerated high knee-lifting steps, and every step goes SQUEAK. He freezes and winces each time. The pirate keeps snoring. The parrot looks bored, flaps over and lands right on the end of the pig's snout.

3–4.5s: The pig's nose wiggles and he sneezes, ACHOO. The pirate's eyes pop open, and pig and pirate scream silently nose to nose with huge cartoon mouths. Both panic, spin and scramble the same way, and BONK, they crash head-first with a big squash-and-stretch right into the web. The red yarn web bursts apart and the strands fly up.

4.5–5s: The strands drop and click into place as one large, correctly formed Traditional Chinese character 蛛 in saturated solid red. On the left is 虫 and on the right is 朱, every stroke clean and separate. The glyph is centered and uncropped, fills about 70% of frame height and has even margins.

5–8s: The glyph holds perfectly still. Pig and pirate sit dazed on either side below it with swirly eyes and goofy grins, then shake hands. The pig peers at the glyph through his magnifier and gives a delighted thumbs-up. The tiny spider lowers itself on a silk thread in the right margin, beside the glyph without touching it, and waves its little legs. The parrot settles on the pirate's head again.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin with Taiwan standard readings, slowly and distinctly, with clear tones and no erhua. The voice reads exactly this line: 蛛、蛛、蜘蛛 (ㄓㄨ、ㄓㄨ、ㄓ ㄓㄨ). Say the first "蛛" at the bonk as the web bursts, at about 3.8s. Say the second "蛛" as the strokes click into the glyph, at about 4.8s. Say "蜘蛛" at about 6s, exactly as the little spider drops down on its thread and waves. Stop after the word. Use only soft squeaks, a sneeze and a gentle bonk as effects, with no music louder than the voice.

The only on-screen text is the single glyph 蛛: no subtitles, no other text, no watermark, no flashing. Use bright, gentle colors, never neon or dark. All characters are stylized cartoon toys.
